answer: The vault multiplier is published, charged in dune, and gale lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4642 identities would post 2429 proofs and burn roughly 23 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
